$comment: Block 20 owner-approved three-basket classification over the Block 14 legacy workflow inventory. Every legacy fact resolves to already-equivalent, release-candidate or post-release; release promotion requires exact replacement evidence, while the default remains post-release.

factPolicy.reason: A legacy fact not named by exact replacement evidence or the focused SC2, Warzone and common Product GA shortlist stays visible after release by default.

releaseCandidateGaps.summary: project.validate exists live in apps/cli/src/project-validation.ts, but its only behavioural test (per-file receipts, fail-closed on unclaimed inputs) was migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/apps/cli/test/cli.test.ts, which vitest.tiers.config.ts excludes as an archived snapshot. Only single-subject subject.validate is proven live through the real CLI process, via the validate-png fixture in scripts/test/command-fixtures-hosts.test.ts.

The claim that the shared CLI validates a positive Galaxy source had its sole test in migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/packages/host/test/language.test.ts, deleted from the live packages/host/test/ tree and excluded from vitest by vitest.tiers.config.ts. COMMAND_FIXTURES in packages/testkit/src/command-fixtures.ts carries no Galaxy fixture, so no live test exercises Galaxy validation through the CLI today.

subject.convert PNG-to-rgba8 is proven live only through the VS Code host (reports/vscode-focused-ga-smoke/receipt.json, scenario focused-positive-conversion). COMMAND_FIXTURES has no 'convert' fixture, so no live test runs subject.convert through the real CLI process the way the archived migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/apps/cli/test/cli.test.ts once did.

The focused-ga smoke receipt's own scenario 'focused-world-presentation' for modkit.previewMap3d shows the installed editor rendering 'The world cannot be rendered: world candidate identity changed between source and info', and the receipt defers semantic proof to apps/web/test/presentation-plan-conformance.test.ts, which exists only in migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/ and is excluded from vitest. Both the direct observation and the deferred proof are currently negative or absent.

reports/vscode-focused-ga-smoke/receipt.json stages m3, pie, SC2Map, wz, odt, png and dds fixtures only. No fixture exercises SC2Layout preview, batch texture conversion, DXT5-to-DXT1, PNG-icon-to-DDS, DDS export-to-PNG, SC2 button-icon prep, audio, video, font, strings-editor or version-file preview, so the generic custom-editor and conversion architecture is unexercised for these eleven legacy facts specifically.

factDecisions.reason: Legacy 'Modkit: Explain mod resolution' explained per-file codec candidates, rejections and the selected offer (see the archived CLI 'explain' behaviour for the shape). The live command of the same name (apps/vscode/src/extension.ts, registerCommand('modkit.explainResolution', ...)) instead reports host topology: extension-host realm, worker realm, webview realm, loaded/refused extension counts and diagnostics count. It is real, registered and exercised in the installed-editor E5 suite (apps/vscode/test-e2e/suite/index.cjs), so the host stays responsive when it runs, but it is a different function under the same command id, not a replacement for per-file resolution explanation. Re-scoped honestly rather than left as already-equivalent on tab presence.
The generic container filesystem, browse command and entry-as-subject flow replace the focused archive opening paths.
The relation graph is a generic data source and a plan-eligible VS Code stage rather than an app-owned command implementation.
A real editor smoke and the six-app recovery matrix prove reload and recovery after a broken update.
Focused games use auto-discovery plus environment and settings overrides; legacy data provisioning is not a Product GA command.
The focused VS Code profile uses the neutral language controller directly; a standalone stdio LSP remains an optional later tool.

The real CLI process validates one subject through subject.validate today (validate-png fixture, scripts/test/command-fixtures-hosts.test.ts, run against apps/cli/dist/main.js). project.validate's whole-project, fail-closed-on-unclaimed-inputs behaviour still exists in source (apps/cli/src/project-validation.ts) but its only test was the archived, non-executing migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/apps/cli/test/cli.test.ts, so that specific claim is unproven live rather than equivalent.

The shared command runtime and CLI process are proven live for other subjects (scripts/test/command-fixtures-hosts.test.ts), so the routing mechanism this fact depends on is real. But the specific claim — validating a positive Galaxy source through subject.validate — has no live fixture: COMMAND_FIXTURES carries no Galaxy entry, and the archived migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/packages/host/test/language.test.ts that once proved it is excluded from vitest and deleted from packages/host/test/.

subject.convert exporting deterministic rgba8 bytes from a PNG is proven live, but only through the VS Code host (reports/vscode-focused-ga-smoke/receipt.json, scenario focused-positive-conversion). No live test runs subject.convert through the real CLI process: COMMAND_FIXTURES has no convert fixture, and the archived migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/apps/cli/test/cli.test.ts that once proved the CLI path specifically is excluded from vitest.

The focused VS Code E5 receipt exercises exactly these facts with real fixtures in a real installed editor: sc2-model.m3 and warzone-model.pie open with the Model stage selected and subject.inspect confirms the formatId (inspectModel, modelViewer, modelViewer.toggle); sc2-map.SC2Map and warzone-map.wz open with the Entries stage selected (previewMap, mapPreview, archiveExplorer); fixture.odt opens with the Tree stage (documentHeaderPreview); texture.png and texture.dds open with the Image stage (previewDds, assetsTextureViewer). Narrowed from the prior 21-unit grouping, which cited the same receipt for eleven facts it does not exercise (see gap-vscode-assets-unexercised-media-and-conversion and gap-vscode-assets-world-render-broken).

The receipt's own scenario for this fact (focused-world-presentation) shows the installed editor's World stage rendering 'The world cannot be rendered: world candidate identity changed between source and info', and defers semantic proof to apps/web/test/presentation-plan-conformance.test.ts, a file that exists only in migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/ and is excluded from vitest. The scenario's PASS verdict checked only that the tab opened and the stage was selected, not that the world actually rendered — exactly the tab-presence check this re-audit was told to stop accepting.

The focused-ga smoke corpus (m3, pie, SC2Map, wz, odt, png, dds) stages no SC2Layout, audio, video, font, strings or version-marked fixture, and exercises only a generic PNG-to-rgba8 conversion, never a batch conversion or a DDS-specific one (DXT5-to-DXT1, PNG-icon-to-DDS, DDS-to-PNG export, SC2 button-icon prep). The same generic custom-editor and stage architecture that already-equivalent facts rely on plausibly extends to these, but nothing in the cited evidence exercises them, so the prior already-equivalent disposition rested on family resemblance rather than a proof for each fact.

apps/vscode/test/game-launch-workflow.test.ts is live and functional: it exercises runExplicitGameLaunch end to end, proving the user-cancel path issues no process grant and does not execute, and the confirmed path issues an exact-map, short-lived process-launch grant scoped to the resource path before executing exactly once. This is the one fact of the former candidate-vscode-authoring group with real behavioural proof; the other nineteen are re-scoped below.

The declarative mapping this group relied on (apps/vscode/src/sc2-authoring-workflows.ts, exporting FOCUSED_SC2_AUTHORING_REPLACEMENTS) no longer exists anywhere outside migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/, and its only test went with it, excluded from vitest. Measured directly: apps/vscode/package.json and its authority bundled-contributes.v1.json both declare 'languages': [], so none of galaxy, ini, sc2layout, sc2strings, sc2style or xml is a live VS Code language contribution today, and none of the thirteen named commands (gamedata.validateMod, gamedata.validateModStrings, openLaunchSettings, openModCard, showEntityCard, showModWiki, strings.extractChanged, strings.openColumns, strings.openText, verifyGalaxyScript, sc2layout.dtree.revealActiveFile/showInTextEditor/showProperties) appears in apps/vscode/src/extension.ts under any name. Whether the underlying function moved into the generic language-session runtime (apps/vscode/src/language-session.ts) or was dropped is unmeasured; recorded as an honest gap rather than left as already-equivalent on a deleted mapping table.
The generic VS Code container workbench provides deterministic search and refresh plus bounded materialization through the shared VFS without app-owned cache semantics.
VS Code now keeps a bounded readable diagnostics journal and exposes native show and export commands instead of relying on an unreadable OutputChannel.

The declarative mapping this group relied on (apps/vscode/src/priority-settings.ts, exporting FOCUSED_PRIORITY_SETTING_REPLACEMENTS with a kind and target per legacy key) no longer exists anywhere outside migration/history/externalization/former-core-tests/, and its only test (priority-settings.test.ts) went with it, excluded from vitest. None of the 25 legacy modkit.* keys appears in apps/vscode/package.json, which is expected under the generic-replacement theory (they were never meant to survive as modkit.* settings) but means no live artifact ties any of the 25 keys to the specific generic setting, provider option, host policy or workflow it was said to become. The live apps/vscode/test/settings.test.ts is real and functional, but it covers a different, generic surface (modkit.extensions, modkit.disabledContributions, modkit.disabledExtensions) — not these 25 keys. Recorded as an honest gap rather than left as already-equivalent on a deleted mapping table.
Native navigation and relation refresh commands operate over the generic relation source and presentation stages that replace the focused MOD tree controls.
The generic provider inventory drives installed-game selection, persisted content-source configuration, validation and unload on top of the proved permission and recovery lifecycle.
All six focused legacy views have one accepted mapping to the native explorer, generic Host and Extensions views, or shared presentation stages.

internalRuntimeCommands.reason: Internal tree action for opening a discovered game source; it is intentionally absent from the public command palette.
Internal tree action for opening a publisher subject card; it is intentionally absent from the public command palette.

Target of the command links a language provider puts in hovers and code lenses (the closed LanguageCommand set, core 6840676d): it runs with the link's arguments, so it has no meaning from the command palette.
Callback of the viewer status-bar items: it receives the item key and the chosen value as arguments, so it has no meaning from the command palette.

packagingBoundary.reason: The accepted Wave 1A package route keeps the deterministic VSIX shell and embeds all eleven catalogued Common roots (lua and java joined the eight codec roots); publisher codecs remain separately managed signed packages.

classification.reason: The focused-ga smoke receipt proves model, map, document and image previews with real fixtures; batch/DDS-specific conversion, SC2Layout preview, audio, video, font, strings-editor and version-file preview are unexercised (gap-vscode-assets-unexercised-media-and-conversion), and the receipt's own World-stage scenario for previewMap3d shows a render error deferred to a now-deleted conformance test (gap-vscode-assets-world-render-broken).

workflows.title: SC2 authoring, language data and launch

classification.reason: Explicit map launch (modkit.launchMap) is proven live and keeps this workflow at already-equivalent by the fact-aggregate rule. The other thirteen commands and all six languages are re-scoped to post-release in candidate-vscode-authoring: the declarative mapping that once justified them (sc2-authoring-workflows.ts) no longer exists live, and apps/vscode/package.json declares zero VS Code languages today.
The generic VFS now covers archive opening, search, refresh and bounded materialization while legacy cache-management utilities remain post-release.

The bounded readable and exportable diagnostics journal replaces the focused log commands and keeps this workflow at already-equivalent by the fact-aggregate rule (candidate-vscode-diagnostics). modkit.explainResolution is re-scoped separately (gap-diagnostics-explain-repurposed): the live command answers with host topology, not the per-file resolution explanation legacy provided under the same id.

candidate-vscode-settings moved to post-release: the declarative mapping that once tied each of the 25 legacy keys to a specific generic setting, provider option, host policy or workflow (priority-settings.ts) no longer exists live, and no live test ties any of the 25 keys to its claimed replacement. None of the 25 keys is expected to survive as a literal modkit.* setting, so their absence from apps/vscode/package.json is not itself the gap; the missing link is proof of where each one actually landed.
Generic native navigation, relation refresh and presentation stages replace the focused MOD tree controls and relation actions.

workflows.title: Thin host shell over the shared subject command runtime

classification.reason: The common subject command runtime and session contract are proven across all required application callers.

Generic provider discovery, installed-game selection, persisted content-source configuration, extension install/update/remove and enable/disable commands, unload, permission handling and recovery form one accepted lifecycle.
All six focused legacy views map exactly once to the native explorer, generic Host and Extensions views, or shared presentation stages.

Single-subject validate through the real CLI process is proven live (scripts/test/command-fixtures-hosts.test.ts). project.validate exists in source (apps/cli/src/project-validation.ts) but its whole-project, fail-closed behaviour has no live test since the archived cli.test.ts was excluded from vitest (gap-cli-check-project-validate).
Focused games use discovery and path overrides; legacy game-data provisioning is not required for Product GA.
The focused VS Code profile uses the neutral language controller; standalone stdio LSP packaging stays post-release.

The shared command runtime is proven live for other subjects. Positive Galaxy validation through the CLI has no live fixture: COMMAND_FIXTURES carries no Galaxy entry, and the archived language.test.ts that once proved it was excluded from vitest and deleted from packages/host/test/ (gap-cli-scripts-galaxy-live-proof).

Positive PNG conversion to rgba8 through subject.convert is proven live only via the VS Code host (reports/vscode-focused-ga-smoke/receipt.json). No live test runs subject.convert through the real CLI process: COMMAND_FIXTURES has no convert fixture, and the archived cli.test.ts that once proved the CLI path was excluded from vitest (gap-cli-texture-convert-live-proof).
